# `secrets/env-file-committed`: Environment file with values is committed (or not gitignored)

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:rules` from the rule metadata in src/rules/. Edit only the
     hand:* regions here; everything else comes from the rule and is overwritten. -->

| Family  | Default severity | GitHub security-severity | CWE                                                                                                                    |
| ------- | ---------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| secrets | high             | 8.0                      | [CWE-538](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/538.html), [CWE-312](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/312.html) |

Individual findings can have a lower or higher severity than the default, and each has a
confidence (high, medium or low). Both are explained below.

## What it detects

<!-- hand:detects -->

Environment files (`.env`, `.env.local`, `.env.production`, …) that contain at least one
non-empty, non-placeholder value and are:

- **tracked by git** (checked with `git ls-files`, so a file that was committed and later
  added to `.gitignore` is still reported, because it is still tracked and in history), or
- **not covered by `.gitignore`** (the next `git add .` would commit it), or
- not gitignored in a directory without a git repository, where VibeGuard cannot confirm
  whether it is committed (reported with that message).

Templates such as `.env.example`, `.env.sample`, `.env.template` and `*.dist` are not
reported.

<!-- /hand:detects -->

## Why it matters

.env files hold the real configuration of an app: database URLs, API keys, signing secrets. When one is tracked by git, every clone, fork and CI cache gets a copy, and it stays in history even after deletion. Adding it to .gitignore afterwards does not untrack it.

## Messages

What a finding from this rule says (parameters in braces):

- {file} is tracked by git and contains {count} non-empty value(s).
- {file} contains {count} value(s) and is not covered by .gitignore; the next "git add ." will commit it.
- {file} contains {count} value(s) and is not covered by .gitignore (no git repository found to confirm whether it is committed).

## How to fix

Rotate every secret in the file first. Then untrack it (git rm --cached `<file>`), add `.env*` with `!.env.example` to .gitignore, and commit a .env.example containing names and placeholders only. If the repository was ever pushed, purge the file from history.

### Vulnerable

```bash
# .gitignore
node_modules
.next
# (.env.local is missing, so "git add ." commits it)
```

### Fixed

```bash
# .gitignore
node_modules
.next
.env*
!.env.example

# then, once:
git rm --cached .env.local
git commit -m "chore: stop tracking .env.local"
```

## False positives and limitations

<!-- hand:false-positives -->

- **Names only or placeholders:** a file with only names or placeholder values has
  nothing to leak and is not reported.
- **Intentionally committed config:** some projects commit a `.env` with public,
  non-secret settings only (for example in a framework template). Prefer renaming it to
  `.env.example` or `.env.defaults`; otherwise suppress it with the reason.
- **No git:** when the project is not a git repository (a zip download), only the
  `.gitignore` check applies.
- **Limitations:** the git index is read locally; whether the file was ever pushed is
  unknown. Removing the file from the working tree does not remove it from history.

<!-- /hand:false-positives -->

## How to suppress

Only suppress a finding after confirming it is safe. Put the directive on the line above
the reported line (or use `vibeguard-ignore-line` on the line itself, or
`vibeguard-ignore-file` anywhere in the file). The reason is required: a directive without
one suppresses nothing and is reported.

```bash
# vibeguard-ignore-file secrets/env-file-committed -- explain why this is safe (at least 10 characters)
NAME=value
```

Use the comment syntax of the file: `//` or `/* */` in code, `#` in `.env` and YAML
files, `--` in SQL.

To turn the rule off or change its severity for the whole project, use `.vibeguard.yml`:

```yaml
version: 1
rules:
  secrets/env-file-committed: off # or: { severity: low }
```

See [configuration](../../configuration.md) and
[ADR-0004](../../adr/0004-suppression-design.md).

## CWE

- [CWE-538](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/538.html): Insertion of Sensitive Information into Externally-Accessible File or Directory
- [CWE-312](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/312.html): Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
